data.title: Rainbow palette from CSS named colors + add neon palette

data.body: Implemented all three plan items. (1) rainbow's 16 swatches replaced with exact CSS named colors — black/dimgray/gray/silver spine, then red, orangered, orange, gold, yellow, lime, green, cyan, blue, indigo, magenta; slot 4 held at #FBFAF8 (not CSS white); tip is now 'rainbow. the css keywords, straight' and the code comment says the values must stay exact. (2) neon added as the sixth palette, appended after rainbow, exact hexes from the plan, 'neon' added to the PaletteId union. (3) BRANDING.md §3: rainbow + neon hex blocks added, count corrected five->six, 'nothing neon' scoped (absolute for shop and all chrome/accent; per-palette departure granted only by the palette's own name), and both carve-outs stated (slot 4 == #FBFAF8 in all six; neon is the one cool spine, with the reason). Two commits: 8e3df57 (code), 5dd5e9a (doc). Verification: npx tsc --noEmit clean, npm run build clean (35 modules, no warnings). Scratchpad smoke harness (not committed) ran 95 checks, all pass: six palettes in order shop/mono/pastel/gem/rainbow/neon with shop first and default; each has exactly 16 valid distinct 6-digit hexes; slot 4 == #FBFAF8 and slot 0 dark in all six; every rainbow non-paper slot asserted equal to its CSS keyword against a hardcoded named-color table; a project encoded with palette 'neon' round-trips through decodeProject, and unknown ('vaporwave') plus absent palette both fall back to shop without rejecting the file; every hex in §3 matches source in both directions, block by block. Deviations: one beyond the plan's letter — the palettes.ts file-header comment said the eleven-color sweep was 'except rainbow', which neon also does now, so it reads 'except rainbow and neon'. No changes to chips UI, stepper, persistence, LCD, chrome, or demo/; the stepper derives its length from PALETTES so it wraps over six unchanged, and app.css's 78px readout width already fits 'rainbow' so 'neon' needs nothing.

Reviewed cold against the plan: commits 8e3df57 (palettes) and 5dd5e9a (BRANDING §3), full text of src/state/palettes.ts, and BRANDING.md §3. Verified with my own harness (scratchpad, not committed; CSS named-color table typed from the spec, not from the implementer's comments), plus a persistence/stepper harness bundled against the real modules via esbuild.

VERDICT: PASS. One trivial doc gap fixed inline (6521110). No implementation-level rework needed.

WHAT PASSED (60+ assertions, 0 fail / 0 warn):
- rainbow slots 0-3 and 5-15 are EXACT CSS named colors, checked in both directions: hex matches the keyword AND the keyword is in the reverse hex->name map (#4B0082 really is indigo, #696969 dimgray, #C0C0C0 silver, #FF4500 orangered, #00FF00 lime vs #008000 green, #FF00FF magenta/fuchsia). No slot other than 4 is absent from the named table. Slot 4 is #FBFAF8, NOT css white #FFFFFF.
- neon matches the plan's 16 hexes byte-for-byte, 16 distinct valid hexes, appended last, and "neon" is in the PaletteId union.
- Slot contract holds in all six: slot 0 relative luminance <= 0.017 everywhere (neon 0.0035), slot 4 == #FBFAF8 in all six, 16/16 unique in all six.
- Stepper derives length from PALETTES (main.ts:453 'const n = PALETTES.length', not a hardcoded 5). Ran it: forward shop->mono->pastel->gem->rainbow->neon->shop, backward shop->neon->...->shop, neon+1 wraps to shop, unknown current id resolves to index 0. shop still default.
- Persistence: all six ids round-trip through encodeProject/decodeProject. Tolerant decode confirmed on 9 hostile inputs (absent key, unknown string, empty, null, number, object, array, wrong case 'NEON', ' neon ' with whitespace) — every one accepted the file and fell back to shop; none returned null.
- BRANDING.md §3: six hex blocks, doc order matches PALETTES order, all six blocks match source hexes exactly in both directions (doc->src and src->doc, no palette in one and not the other), count corrected, zero stale 'five' anywhere in the file.
- Scope clean: only BRANDING.md and src/state/palettes.ts touched. chips UI, stepper, persist logic, LCD, chrome, demo untouched. tsc --noEmit clean, npm run build clean.

DOC PROSE JUDGMENT: the 'Where "nothing neon" applies' paragraph reads as a deliberate rule, not a patch — it names the absolute domain (shop + chrome), grants the licence, then bounds it three ways (per-palette, granted by the name, never chrome or accent) and closes the drift hole with 'It is not a licence to brighten the other four.' 'licence' is British but so is 'centre' throughout src/, so that is consistent, not a typo.

DESIGN JUDGMENT ON NEON — sound, ships as-is:
- Ordered sweep confirmed: hues 344 -> 25 -> 50 -> 73 -> 111 -> 167 -> 186 -> 202 -> 235 -> 278 -> 306, monotonic once unwrapped (-16 -> 306). Genuine sweep, same logic as rainbow.
- Distinctness at 19px is fine. Min pairwise dE2000 among the eleven colors is 12.7 (#C6FF00/#39FF14); min adjacent is also 12.7. That is on par with the shipped house set (shop's min is 13.4, #2E5FD2/#7B4FD2). Neon is no more crowded than shop.
- Spine slot0->slot1 is dE00 9.7 (#0B0B12 -> #1E1B2E), close, but gem already ships 8.4 at the same position. Not an outlier, not worth changing.

RISK I AM FLAGGING (accepted, not a defect):
rainbow slot 6 #FF4500 orangered is dE2000 1.7 from the brand accent #FF4E00 — below the just-noticeable threshold, i.e. the same color at 19px. tokens.css calls the accent 'the only one'. Two real consequences: (1) when that chip is the current color its aria-pressed ring is var(--orange) at 2px offset, so the ring reads as a faint halo rather than a contrast ring; (2) rainbow's red and orangered are dE00 6.4 apart, the closest adjacent pair in any shipped palette, and read as two reds side by side. Neither is fixable chromatically — orangered IS the CSS keyword and the plan rightly forbids retuning it, so the honest response is documentary. I judged this a doc gap rather than a code defect: §3 asserted the accent stays reserved without admitting a chip now lands on it.
FIX APPLIED (6521110, doc only, no swatch/code/behavior change): added a paragraph to §3's rainbow entry naming the collision, explaining why the accent keeps its meaning (orange signifies by where it appears, not by hex exclusivity), and naming both costs so the next reader does not rediscover them as bugs. Re-ran the full harness and the build after the edit — still 0 fail / 0 warn, build clean.
Secondary, no action: neon's #FF6B00 is dE00 6.9 from the accent — noticeable but distinguishable, and it is a canvas chip on a dark set rather than chrome.

All acceptance criteria in the plan are met.
